source_title: What Should FuelCell Energy, Inc. Investors Know After 15.69% Stock Drop? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline
source_excerpt:
Lawsuit alleges FuelCell Energy, Inc. made misleading statements to investors from June 24, 2026 to September 1, 2026; lead plaintiff motions are due November 10, 2026
LOS ANGELES , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz today announced a class action lawsuit against FuelCell Energy, Inc. ("FuelCell" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: FCEL ) on behalf of investors who acquired the Company's securities from June 24, 2026 to September 1, 2026. Filed on September 11, 2026, the case is Nguyen v. FuelCell Energy, Inc. et al. , U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, Case No. 26-cv-07953.
If you lost money on FuelCell Energy, Inc. securities, submit your FuelCell Energy, Inc. loss information by November 10, 2026 to learn about participating in the lawsuit.
FuelCell Energy, Inc. class action timeline
Lead plaintiff motion deadline: November 10, 2026
On September 2, 2026, FuelCell reported its fiscal third-quarter results. The Company reported, among other things, that revenue fell 29% year over year to $33 million, primarily due to lower product sales caused by fewer module deliveries to customers in South Korea. FuelCell further reported it saw a gross loss from product revenues for the quarter reflecting that product costs and manufacturing overhead currently exceeded the contractual pricing established under the Fit Energy agreement . FuelCell recognized approximately $17 million in charges related to the initial 30 MW phase of that agreement.
On this news, FuelCell shares fell $2.68 or 15.69% to close at $14.40 on September 2, 2026, thereby injuring investors.
What is the FuelCell Energy, Inc. lawsuit about?
The FuelCell Energy, Inc. securities lawsuit alleges that, between June 24, 2026 and September 1, 2026, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about FuelCell Energy, Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose that: (1) the Company's manufacturing capacity was inadequate to generate the production rate required under the CEPA; (2) as a result, the Company's annualized production rate for deliveries under the CEPA with Fit Energy was slower than expected; (3) as a result, the Company was incurring higher product costs and manufacturing overhead expenses; (4) as a result of the slower production rate, the Company was reasonably likely to incur charges in connection with the CEPA; (5) the foregoing was a known trend affecting the Company's profitability; and (6) as a result, defendants' positive statements about FuelCell Energy, Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.
" According to the complaint filed against FuelCell Energy, Inc., the Company, among other things, did not disclose that the Company's manufacturing capacity was inadequate to generate the production rate required under the CEPA. The November 10, 2026 deadline is a key date for FuelCell Energy, Inc. investors who want a voice in how this case moves forward, " said Frank R. Cruz of The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz.
What should FuelCell Energy, Inc. investors do now?
The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz can help FuelCell Energy, Inc. investors evaluate potential claims to recover their losses.
Investors who want to serve as lead plaintiff in the FuelCell Energy, Inc. class action must file a motion with the Court by November 10, 2026. For more information, visit the FuelCell Energy, Inc. case page , email [email protected] , or call 310-914-5007.
If you inquire by email, please include your mailing address, telephone number, and number of shares purchased.
Investors may retain counsel of their choice. FuelCell Energy, Inc. investors who bought during the class period may also take no action and remain absent class members. No class has been certified yet in the FuelCell Energy, Inc. case.
Questions and answers about the FuelCell Energy, Inc. lawsuit
Who is eligible? Investors who bought FuelCell Energy, Inc. securities between June 24, 2026 and September 1, 2026 and lost money may be class members, and may seek lead plaintiff appointment by November 10, 2026.
What does a lead plaintiff do? The lead plaintiff is appointed by the court to represent all class members and direct the FuelCell Energy, Inc. class action.
Must I be lead plaintiff to share in a recovery? No, FuelCell Energy, Inc. investors can take no action and remain absent class members.
How are attorneys' fees handled? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz works on contingency, so FuelCell Energy, Inc. investors pay no attorneys' fees up front. Any attorneys' fees and litigation expenses come only from a recovery, if there is one, and require court approval.
